events.title: Henry VIII Recognized as Supreme Head of the Church of England
events.description: The English clergy acknowledged King Henry VIII as supreme head of the Church of England. This was a decisive step in his break with Rome.
events.significance: It laid the groundwork for the English Reformation and permanently reshaped the religious and political identity of England.

events.title: Bernadette Soubirous Reports the First Vision at Lourdes
events.description: Fourteen-year-old Bernadette Soubirous, a peasant girl, reported the first of eighteen apparitions of the Virgin Mary near the town of Lourdes in southern France.
events.significance: Lourdes became one of the world's most visited Catholic pilgrimage sites, drawing millions of visitors each year.

events.title: General Motors Recognizes the United Auto Workers
events.description: After a sit-down strike that lasted weeks, General Motors agreed to recognize the United Auto Workers union.
events.significance: The settlement was a landmark victory for organized labor and opened the way for union organizing across American industry.

events.title: Iran's Islamic Revolution Reaches Its Climax
events.description: The revolution in Iran reached its turning point, and the old monarchy's government fell to forces loyal to Ayatollah Khomeini.
events.significance: The revolution replaced a centuries-old monarchy with an Islamic republic and changed the geopolitics of the Middle East.

events.title: Buster Douglas Stuns Mike Tyson
events.description: Buster Douglas, a 42-to-1 underdog, knocked out Mike Tyson in Tokyo. It was Tyson's first professional loss, and Douglas became the undisputed heavyweight champion.
events.significance: It is widely regarded as one of the greatest upsets in boxing history and in sports generally.
